name: semantic-identifiability certificate
definition: For a declared finite candidate-mapping audit set O and a signed contrast delta(o), the envelope is [min_o delta(o), max_o delta(o)]. Effect direction is identified only when this interval excludes zero.
schema_basis: The paper band listing and official display give RGBN stronger release-internal support. BGRN is retained as a lower-support native-product sensitivity because array-construction/reordering provenance is absent; equal plausibility is not assigned.

contrasts.estimand: candidate-index attention minus raw-edge attention mean F1
contrasts.interpretation: The candidate index is not superior to the same-capacity raw edge control under either declared candidate mapping.

contrasts.estimand: equal-mass index modulation minus plain boundary weighting mean F1
contrasts.interpretation: Index modulation is inferior on mean F1 under both declared candidate mappings.

contrasts.estimand: equal-mass index modulation minus plain boundary weighting mean boundary F1
contrasts.interpretation: The boundary-effect direction is not semantically identifiable because its envelope crosses zero.

contrasts.estimand: plain boundary weighting minus base loss, mean across three attention controls and three seeds
contrasts.interpretation: The generic boundary effect is positive under both mappings and in all 18 individual comparisons.

scope: Finite sensitivity certificate for two evidentially asymmetric candidate mappings; not a population interval, equal-plausibility claim, or proof that the set is exhaustive.
